title: Philippine-Chinese clashes spike across the South China Sea
deck: At least six dangerous encounters in nine days, a new flashpoint off northern Luzon and a Chinese carrier group circling the Philippines put Manila, Beijing and Washington on a collision course just before Trump meets Xi in Shenzhen.
region: Philippines, South China Sea, Luzon Strait

fuel.title: Liaoning group shadowed off Mindanao
fuel.how: China's carrier group sails near the southern Philippines while a US carrier group exercises in the same waters, and a new Philippine Coast Guard vessel shadows the Chinese group, so forces are in close contact at sea.

fuel.title: Hegseth to visit Manila as rhetoric hardens
fuel.how: A Philippine official dares China to 'do what you want' and the US defense secretary is due in the Philippines, which hardens positions on both sides.

card.headline: The South China Sea is hotter than at any point this year, and the heat now reaches the Luzon Strait

keyNumber.label: dangerous Philippine-Chinese encounters between 1 and 9 October, at four separate areas

forYou.line: No commercial disruption is reported so far. Watch Scarborough Shoal, the Spratlys and the Luzon Strait for any move toward exclusion zones or blockades.
A Chinese carrier group, a US carrier exercise and a Philippine coast guard shadowing ship are all in the same waters. Close contact raises the risk of an accident.
Markets have not been shown to react. The real test is whether Trump's 18-19 November meeting with Xi in Shenzhen calms or inflames the sea.
Fishers near Scarborough and off Batanes face the most direct risk. Church leaders in the Philippines are urging safety for fishermen.
Taiwan's coast guard has now appeared in the Luzon Strait. That ties Manila's dispute to the Taiwan question.

effects.text: At least six dangerous encounters at Scarborough Shoal, Second Thomas Shoal, the Spratlys and off Batanes between 1 and 9 October
A PLA J-16 fighter closes on a Philippine Cessna 208 on 3 October; Chinese ships block a Philippine patrol within 9 metres on 4 October
China Coast Guard harassment delays a medevac from BRP Sierra Madre; in September Beijing blocked a resupply for the first time since the June 2024 provisional arrangement
Official rhetoric hardens: a Philippine official tells China to 'do what you want'; US Defense Secretary Hegseth is due in the Philippines for ASEAN defence events
The 2024 resupply understanding looks fragile, and the Sierra Madre outpost becomes the likeliest place for an incident
The Luzon Strait becomes a new flashpoint, with Taiwan sending three coast guard boats as a China Coast Guard cutter escorts a survey ship
Chinese and US carrier groups operate in the western Pacific at the same time, and a Philippine coast guard vessel shadows the Chinese group
Manila leans harder on Washington and other partners, such as Italy, for diplomatic and security support
Beijing hosts Trump at APEC in Shenzhen on 18-19 November, so continued coast guard pressure tests whether summitry restrains Chinese behaviour at sea
Pressure on US-allied frontline states grows at the same time on the Korean peninsula, as Trump pursues deals with both Xi and Kim
A serious accident or death would put the US-Philippine Mutual Defense Treaty and US credibility under test
Insurers, shipowners and fishing fleets may start to price in a persistently contested route and fishing grounds (our estimate; nothing reported yet)

whatHappened: Between 1 and 9 October 2026, Philippine and Chinese forces had at least six dangerous encounters. They took place at Scarborough Shoal, Second Thomas Shoal, in the Spratly Islands and at a new flashpoint off Batanes in the Luzon Strait. On 3 October a Chinese PLA J-16 fighter closed on a Philippine Cessna 208 patrol aircraft. On 4 October Chinese ships blocked a Philippine patrol within 9 metres. China Coast Guard harassment also delayed a medevac from BRP Sierra Madre, the Philippine outpost on Second Thomas Shoal.

In September Beijing blocked a Sierra Madre resupply mission for the first time since the June 2024 provisional arrangement that had calmed the shoal. Off Batanes, a China Coast Guard cutter escorted a survey ship near an exclusive economic zone, and Taiwan sent three coast guard boats to the area.

The pressure carried into late October. A Chinese carrier group led by the Liaoning passed near the southern Philippines while the USS Theodore Roosevelt group exercised in the Philippine Sea. A new Philippine Coast Guard vessel shadowed the Chinese group off Mindanao. A Philippine official told China to 'do what you want' as the diplomatic exchange sharpened, and US Defense Secretary Hegseth was reported to be heading to the Philippines for ASEAN defence ministers' events.
whyItMatters: Security: this is gray-zone pressure, meaning coercion without open war, and it is spreading geographically. Scarborough, Second Thomas and the Spratlys are long-running hotspots. The Luzon Strait is newer and sits between the Philippines and Taiwan. When a carrier group, a US carrier exercise and a coast guard ship that is shadowing the Chinese group all operate in the same waters, a small mistake could turn into a larger incident. The September resupply block also suggests the 2024 understanding is weaker than assumed. Nothing in the reporting shows a shot fired or anyone killed.

Politics: both sides are hardening in public. Manila's tone is defiant and Washington is signalling backing through Hegseth's visit. Beijing hosts Trump at the APEC summit in Shenzhen on 18-19 November, after Xi's state visit to Washington ended on 25 September with a declared 'constructive relationship of strategic stability'. If coast guard pressure continues while Beijing plays host, summitry is not changing behaviour at sea. If it eases, the summit may be restraining China. North Korea's missile tests are a separate driver, but they also put US-allied frontline states under pressure ahead of Trump's November Asia trip.

winners.who: Naval and defence planners in the region
winners.why: Carrier deployments, patrols and shadowing missions strengthen the case for more ships, aircraft and surveillance spending.
Coast guard and PLA pressure has so far met no costly response; coercion is working in the near term (our judgement).
Hegseth's visit and a US carrier exercise nearby show Washington's commitment and give Manila diplomatic cover.

losers.who: Philippine fishers and coast guard crews
losers.why: They face harassment and close passes at sea, and a medevac from Sierra Madre has already been delayed.
Resupply is blocked or impeded for the first time since the 2024 arrangement.
A cohesive ASEAN response is harder when two members are in a public war of words and a third is drawn in through the Luzon Strait.

losers.who: Anyone hoping summitry would calm the sea
losers.why: Pressure continues despite the run-up to Shenzhen.

whatsNext: 29 October: the Keen Sword exercise in the Philippine Sea is due to run through this date, per one report.
Date not stated in the material: Hegseth visits the Philippines for ASEAN defence ministers' events.
Next Sierra Madre resupply: the main test of whether Beijing allows the 2024 arrangement to hold.
18-19 November: APEC leaders meet in Shenzhen, with Trump expected to attend.
Late November: Trump may meet Kim Jong Un during the Asia trip, and North Korea's missile tests are a parallel pressure.

predict.question: Before you read the scenarios: what do you think is the most likely path through the 18-19 November Shenzhen summit?
options: Gray-zone pressure continues at a lower, steadier level
A visible lull as Beijing tries to look like a stable host
A serious accident or casualty at sea
A formal US-China understanding on the South China Sea
predict.explanation: Our base case, at about 50%, is continued gray-zone pressure at a similar or slightly lower level, with periodic incidents and no deaths. A temporary lull is the second most likely path at about 25%. A serious accident is about 20%.

timeline.title: Arbitral tribunal rules on the Philippines' case
timeline.detail: The tribunal at The Hague largely rejects China's sweeping South China Sea claims. Beijing says it does not accept the ruling. General background, not from the cited sources.

timeline.title: Clash at Second Thomas Shoal
timeline.detail: A resupply run ended in a violent confrontation that injured Filipino personnel. A provisional arrangement on resupply followed in June 2024, as described in the event material.

timeline.title: Beijing blocks a Sierra Madre resupply
timeline.detail: The first block since the June 2024 provisional arrangement. The exact day is not given in the material; the date shown is a placeholder for September.

timeline.title: Xi's state visit to Washington ends
timeline.detail: The two sides declare a 'constructive relationship of strategic stability', with few concrete trade deliverables. Context from the connected APEC dossier.

timeline.title: PLA J-16 closes on a Philippine Cessna 208
timeline.detail: A Chinese fighter jet approaches a Philippine patrol aircraft, one of at least six dangerous encounters in nine days.

timeline.title: Chinese ships block a Philippine patrol within 9 metres
timeline.detail: Manila accuses China of harassing patrols in disputed waters; AFP reports the claims.

timeline.title: Incidents spike across four areas, including Batanes
timeline.detail: A China Coast Guard cutter escorts a survey ship near an EEZ off Batanes. Taiwan sends three coast guard boats. A Sierra Madre medevac is delayed by harassment.

timeline.title: Liaoning group passes near the southern Philippines
timeline.detail: China's carrier and its escorts operate in waters where a US carrier group is also exercising. One report counts 288 missile cells among the Chinese escorts.

timeline.title: Manila-Beijing word war escalates
timeline.detail: A Philippine official dares China to 'do what you want'.

timeline.title: Philippine coast guard vessel shadows Chinese carrier group
timeline.detail: A new coast guard ship follows the Chinese strike group off Mindanao, putting the two sides in close contact. Hegseth is also reported to be heading to the Philippines.

causes.name: Overlapping claims
causes.detail: China claims most of the South China Sea. The Philippines claims features and waters inside its own EEZ. The 2016 tribunal ruling went Manila's way, but Beijing rejects it.

causes.name: The Sierra Madre outpost
causes.detail: The Philippines keeps a ship grounded on Second Thomas Shoal as a military outpost. China wants it gone, so every resupply is a potential confrontation.

causes.name: US-China rivalry
causes.detail: The Philippines is a US treaty ally, so any serious incident draws in Washington. Taiwan's location just north of Luzon adds another link.

causes.name: First resupply block since the 2024 arrangement
causes.detail: Beijing's September block removed the main rule that had been reducing friction at Second Thomas Shoal.

causes.name: A burst of coordinated pressure
causes.detail: Six dangerous encounters in nine days across four areas suggest a deliberate campaign, though the sources do not say why it began now.

causes.name: A new northern flashpoint
causes.detail: The Batanes encounter, with a China Coast Guard cutter escorting a survey ship and Taiwan sending coast guard boats, links the Philippine dispute to the Taiwan question.

causes.name: Naval build-up
causes.detail: A Chinese carrier group circling the Philippines at the same time as a US carrier exercise raises the chance of a collision.

causes.name: Hardening rhetoric
causes.detail: Public defiance from Manila and a visit from Hegseth make backing down costlier for both sides.

causes.name: Summit calendar
causes.detail: With Trump due in Shenzhen on 18-19 November, each side has an incentive to look strong, and the timing may also be shaping Beijing's choices (our judgement).

stakeholders.name: Philippine government (Marcos administration)
stakeholders.wants: Keep the Sierra Madre supplied, protect fishers and patrols, and defend its EEZ without a shooting war
stakeholders.leverage: Public transparency about incidents, new coast guard ships, and the US alliance
stakeholders.likelyMove: Keep publicising Chinese harassment, keep shadowing missions and seek more international partners

stakeholders.name: China Coast Guard and PLA
stakeholders.role: Chinese enforcement at sea and in the air
stakeholders.wants: Establish control over disputed features and discourage Philippine and foreign activity
stakeholders.leverage: Larger numbers of ships and aircraft, and the ability to turn the pressure up or down
stakeholders.likelyMove: Continue gray-zone pressure while avoiding a clear act of war, possibly easing before 18-19 November

stakeholders.name: Taiwan
stakeholders.role: Neighbour with its own stake in the Luzon Strait
stakeholders.wants: Show presence and keep the strait from becoming a Chinese-controlled lane
stakeholders.leverage: Coast guard boats and diplomatic signalling
stakeholders.likelyMove: Keep modest, visible coast guard patrols and coordinate informally with Manila

stakeholders.name: United States (Hegseth and the Pentagon)
stakeholders.wants: Reassure Manila and deter China without being drawn into an incident before the Shenzhen summit
stakeholders.leverage: Carrier presence, the Mutual Defense Treaty, military cooperation
stakeholders.likelyMove: Visible backing at ASEAN defence events and naval exercises, with no new binding commitments

stakeholders.name: Donald Trump and Xi Jinping
stakeholders.role: Leaders meeting at APEC in Shenzhen on 18-19 November
stakeholders.wants: Trump: trade and other deals. Xi: tariff relief and a stable-host image
stakeholders.leverage: Control of the summit agenda (Xi) and US tariff and security policy (Trump)
stakeholders.likelyMove: Both keep the sea off the main agenda unless an incident forces it on

stakeholders.name: ASEAN
stakeholders.role: Regional bloc hosting the defence ministers' events
stakeholders.wants: A code of conduct and stability among its members
stakeholders.likelyMove: Call for restraint and dialogue while members split over how hard to press China

stakeholders.name: Philippine fishers and church leaders
stakeholders.leverage: Public moral pressure; headlines show Catholic leaders urging both firmness and peace
stakeholders.likelyMove: Keep calling for peaceful, firm defence of the West Philippine Sea

sectors.why: Carrier deployments, shadowing missions and aircraft intercepts strengthen the case for more ships, aircraft and surveillance in the region.
Blocked or delayed Sierra Madre resupply and a delayed medevac raise the cost and risk of keeping the outpost supplied.
Harassment near Scarborough and Spratly features makes fishing riskier for Filipino crews. Church leaders have urged safety for fishermen amid the Chinese buildup.

No disruption to commercial traffic is reported. A frequently cited estimate puts roughly a third of global maritime trade through the South China Sea, so any shift would matter. Risk premiums may creep up if incidents spread to commercial lanes (our estimate).
Manila is seeking deeper ties with partners such as Italy, which helps it. A word war with Beijing, and a tougher ASEAN meeting, hurts it.
Taiwan's coast guard presence near Batanes shows closer coordination of interests, but it also gives Beijing a reason to frame the Luzon Strait as part of the Taiwan question.

dailyLife.effect: Fishers near contested features face the most direct risk. Church leaders in the Philippines have urged their safety amid the Chinese buildup.
No effect on consumer prices has been reported so far. A real disruption would show up first in shipping and insurance costs, which we do not yet see.

dailyLife.item: News and public mood in the Philippines
dailyLife.effect: Defiant rhetoric from officials and church statements are keeping the dispute at the centre of public debate.
No airspace closures are reported. Military aircraft intercepts, like the J-16 pass at a Cessna 208, are a risk to patrol flights, not commercial ones.

scenarios.name: Simmering gray-zone pressure
scenarios.looksLike: Incidents continue at a similar pace with no deaths. The 2024 arrangement frays but survives in some form, and carrier groups leave after exercises.
signposts: More reports of water cannon, blocking and close air passes
scenarios.effectOnWorld: The sea stays a permanent source of friction, and Manila keeps drawing in partners.

scenarios.name: Summit-driven lull
scenarios.looksLike: Beijing eases pressure before and during the Shenzhen summit to look like a stable host. Incidents drop in number, though not to zero.
scenarios.effectOnWorld: Evidence that summitry can restrain behaviour at sea, though the pause may only last until the summit ends.

scenarios.name: Serious accident or casualty
scenarios.looksLike: A collision, injury or death at Scarborough, Second Thomas or in the Luzon Strait. Manila and Washington consult, and Beijing blames Manila.
signposts: A ship collision or a medevac that cannot reach the outpost
Aircraft intercept at under tens of metres
US officials speak of treaty obligations
scenarios.effectOnWorld: A sharp rise in tension that could disrupt the summit, move markets and test the US-Philippine treaty.

scenarios.name: Open crisis
scenarios.looksLike: A blockade of the Sierra Madre or a standoff in the Luzon Strait that involves Taiwan and the US directly.
signposts: US carrier moves toward the contested area
Taiwan and the Philippines coordinate operations
scenarios.effectOnWorld: Shipping and trade reroute or pause, markets sell off and the summit is likely cancelled or overshadowed.

predictions.text: At least one more publicly reported dangerous Philippine-Chinese encounter will occur between 27 October and 18 November (about 85% likely).
No one will be killed in a Philippine-Chinese encounter at sea by the end of 2026 (about 90% likely).
China will block or impede at least one more Sierra Madre resupply or medevac by year-end (about 50% likely).
Trump will publicly raise the South China Sea or the Philippines in Shenzhen or in remarks around the summit (about 25% likely).
The Philippines will not formally invoke the Mutual Defense Treaty with the US (about 97% likely).

actions: Track Scarborough Shoal, the Spratlys and the Luzon Strait on shipping risk dashboards.
Review insurance and contract clauses for routes through the South China Sea.
Prepare contingency routing for cargo to and from the Philippines and Taiwan.
Treat this as a persistent political-risk factor, not a one-off shock.
Watch the 18-19 November summit for any change in tone before assuming a calmer period.
Look at defence, shipping and insurance exposure; no market move has yet been shown.
Expect no direct price effect unless shipping lanes are disrupted.
Follow official advice if you live or work in coastal northern Luzon or fishing communities.
Check travel advisories for areas near Batanes and the Spratlys.
Keep Sierra Madre resupply open and publicise obstruction.
Coordinate with the US and Taiwan on incident communications to avoid accidents.
Use the Shenzhen summit window to seek a crisis hotline or incident rules.

analogues.whatFollowed: After a weeks-long face-off, Chinese vessels stayed and the Philippines lost practical access; background knowledge, not from the cited sources.

analogues.event: HD-981 oil rig standoff with Vietnam
analogues.whatFollowed: China parked a drilling rig in disputed waters for weeks, ships collided and the rig was withdrawn; coercion continued afterwards in other forms.

analogues.event: Second Thomas Shoal clash and provisional arrangement
analogues.whatFollowed: A violent incident in June 2024 led to an arrangement that reduced resupply confrontations until September 2026.

watch.title: Keen Sword exercise end date
watch.why: One report says the US carrier exercise runs through 29 October. Chinese carrier movements after it ends will show whether this was a one-off.

watch.title: Hegseth's Philippines visit
watch.why: The date is not given in the material. His statements on the treaty will show how firmly Washington backs Manila.

watch.title: Next Sierra Madre resupply
watch.why: Whether it is blocked, delayed or allowed is the cleanest test of the 2024 arrangement.

watch.title: APEC leaders' meeting, Shenzhen (18-19 November)
watch.why: Watch whether pressure eases before it and whether the leaders mention the sea.

watch.title: Luzon Strait and Batanes
watch.why: More Taiwanese or Chinese coast guard activity would confirm a second theatre.

watch.title: North Korea's missile tests and Trump's possible Kim meeting
watch.why: A parallel pressure on US allies that may shape how Washington handles both summits.

watch.title: Philippine-Chinese statements
watch.why: Further public defiance or a diplomatic summons would signal a harder line or a break in talks.

confidence.claim: At least six dangerous encounters between 1 and 9 October, including the J-16 intercept and the 9-metre blocking
confidence.note: From the USNI News report of 9 October and AFP reporting of 4 October; both rely on Philippine accounts.

confidence.claim: Beijing blocked a Sierra Madre resupply in September for the first time since the June 2024 arrangement
confidence.note: Taken from the event summary; the exact day and Chinese account are not in the material.

confidence.claim: Taiwan sent three coast guard boats off Batanes as a China Coast Guard cutter escorted a survey ship near an EEZ
confidence.note: From the event summary; the material does not say whose EEZ, and Taiwan's and China's views are not shown.

confidence.claim: The Liaoning group is passing near the southern Philippines while a US carrier group exercises nearby, and a Philippine coast guard ship shadows it
confidence.note: Based on headlines from USNI News, 19FortyFive, Marine Insight and the SCMP; full articles were not read. The 288 missile cell figure comes from a headline only.

confidence.claim: Hegseth will visit the Philippines for ASEAN defence events
confidence.note: Headline-level information from the SCMP via UA.NEWS; no visit date is given.

confidence.claim: Links to the APEC summit and North Korea's missile tests
confidence.note: Taken from the connected dossiers as judged; the causal links are indirect and no source says either event caused the other.
Author judgement, not sourced forecasts; to be graded as events resolve.

confidence.claim: Background points (2016 ruling, 2012 and 2014 standoffs, share of global trade through the sea)
confidence.note: General knowledge, not cited to a source; stated cautiously and not used for headline claims.

evidence.method: Drafted from the listed sources, the matched headlines and the connected dossiers on APEC and North Korea. Only two of the sources are full articles with usable URLs on the event; the late-October developments (the Liaoning group, the coast guard shadowing, the rhetoric and the Hegseth visit) come from headlines and short summaries, so details such as dates and scale are limited. Because the material supports only two parts of the economy, security and politics, the fuel section has two entries rather than three or more. Scenario probabilities, predictions and the sector and everyday-life effects are estimates by the author.
